summary: This Part II builds the finite integral dominance and diagram-folding direction above the existing root-system roadmap. It supplies one integral order, the Stembridge step, all finite orbit-sum folds including adjacent even A and component cycles, and the invariant coroot-step export with central directions retained. Two independent routed directions receive exhaustive split briefs and stable item assignments rather than incomplete mathematical nodes.

nodes.title: Integral root dominance
nodes.statement: For x,y in the weight space, RootLE(Δ,x,y) means y−x ∈ TauCeti.posRootCone(Φ,Δ). On L this is integral root dominance. Coroot dominance is this very definition for the flipped pairing and flipped base. No global order instance is imposed on the ambient module.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
proofSteps: Wrap the existing additive submonoid; reflexivity and transitivity use zero and addition in it.
Pointedness gives antisymmetry. Simple-root independence gives the coefficientwise criterion when both differences are in Q.
Restrict to L or its σ-fixed subgroup without changing the cone. The rational cone is used only for a comparison implication.

nodes.title: Stembridge positive-root step
nodes.statement: For distinct dominant integral λ,μ∈L with RootLE(λ,μ), there is β∈Φ⁺ with λ+β dominant and RootLE(λ+β,μ). Consequently λ<_Qλ+β≤_Qμ. This assertion remains valid in an ambient weight space with central directions: its proof uses only the simple-coroot tests.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
proofSteps: Write μ−λ=Σ n_i α_i. Positive roots with coordinates m_i≤n_i form a finite nonempty set: a simple root with n_i>0 belongs to it. Choose a maximal member β in the integral root order.

For each simple α_i, maximality implies either β+α_i is not a root or m_i=n_i. If the sum is not a root, the contrapositive of the obtuse-sum lemma, with the nonopposite-root hypothesis checked, gives ⟨β,α_i∨⟩≥0.
If m_i=n_i, write λ+β=μ−Σ_(j≠i)(n_j−m_j)α_j and use dominance of μ and nonpositive off-diagonal Cartan entries. This proves every simple-coroot inequality.
The remaining coefficients n_i−m_i give the upper bound; β is positive and nonzero, so pointedness makes the lower bound strict. Integrality and membership in L follow from Q⊆L.

nodes.title: Folding with orthogonal simple orbits
nodes.statement: Assume Φ is finite and simply laced and any two distinct simple roots in one σ-orbit are orthogonal. On E^σ, the set Ψ={OrbitSum(σ,α):α∈Φ}, with duplicates removed, is a finite reduced crystallographic root system with base B={β_O:O a simple orbit}. The form is the restricted canonical positive form, with positive componentwise rescaling constant on σ-cycles when normalizing lengths. Such rescaling leaves all coroot pairings unchanged. With original roots normalized to squared length 2, (β_O,β_O)=2|O| and ⟨β_O,β_T∨⟩=−N_OT/|T| for O≠T, where N_OT counts edges between the two blocks.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
Φ is simply laced on each component, with the normalization constant across components permuted by σ.
Simple σ-orbits are pairwise orthogonal within each orbit.
proofSteps: The sums β_O are linearly independent and span the fixed space: invariant simple coefficients are constant on orbits. Counting neighbors at a fixed node of T proves the displayed Cartan entries are integers and nonpositive.
For each O, the commuting product ∏_(i∈O)s_i restricts to reflection in β_O. These products preserve the set of root-orbit sums.

Descend the positive height of a root-orbit sum by such reflections using positive definiteness. If all resulting orbit roots become negative, the original orbit consists of the simple roots of that block. Thus every orbit sum is in the reflection orbit of a β_O.

Conversely those reflection orbits are orbit sums. This gives the generated finite root system, its base, reducedness and crystallographic axiom; Stembridge Claim 4 also proves all original root orbits are orthogonal under these finite hypotheses.

nodes.title: Weyl group of an orthogonal fold
nodes.statement: For the orthogonal fold, restriction gives an isomorphism W(Φ)^σ ≃ W(Ψ). Its inverse sends the simple reflection of β_O to ∏_(i∈O)s_i. Here W(Φ)^σ is the fixed subgroup under conjugation by σ, not the pointwise stabilizer of E^σ.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
The hypotheses of orthogonal-fold hold.
proofSteps: The reflection comparison proves that the block products act as the folded simple reflections.

For a nonidentity fixed w choose a simple inversion using the pinned simple-descent theorem. Its entire simple σ-orbit consists of inversions. The reflections in that block commute and fix the other simple roots of the block, so each successive multiplication removes one inversion, by the pinned inversion-cardinality theorem. The total drop is |O|. The block product is fixed by σ; induct on inversion cardinality. No unplanned parabolic normal-form theorem is used.

Restriction is injective on the fixed subgroup: choose a strictly dominant vector and sum its finite σ-orbit to get a strictly dominant fixed vector. Existence of the first vector follows by solving the nonsingular simple-coroot matrix on E. An element trivial on E^σ fixes this vector, so the existing chamber stabilizer theorem and empty-wall theorem imply that element is identity. Restriction contains every folded simple reflection and every fixed element is a product of block reflections, giving the isomorphism.

nodes.title: Adjacent folding of even A type
nodes.statement: For n≥1, realize A_(2n) in the coordinate-sum-zero subspace of R^(2n+1), with σ(e_a−e_b)=e_(2n+2−b)−e_(2n+2−a). Put f_i=e_i−e_(2n+2−i), 1≤i≤n. The distinct orbit sums are exactly {±f_i, ±f_i±f_j : i<j}; their base is f_i−f_(i+1) (i<n), f_n. This is the B_n root model, with the rank-one case identified directly with A1. Every f_i has squared norm 2.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, with base Δ; rank zero is allowed.
A chosen integral subgroup L satisfies Q(Φ) ⊆ L and every coroot takes integral values on L. Dominance is the existing closed simple-coroot chamber.
The based irreducible system is A_(2n) and σ is its nonidentity reversal. Coordinate indices here are one-based.
proofSteps: Transport (Φ,Δ,σ) to the pinned model. By diagram-automorphism-orbits Φ has type A_(2n) and σ reverses the numbered simple roots. RootPairing.Base.equivOfCartanMatrixEq along that numbering identifies Φ with the real base change of TauCeti.DynkinType.typeASimplyConnectedRootDatum (2n), base to base. Over ℝ that base change spans, its simple roots being the rows of the invertible Cartan matrix, and its base and reducedness come from the pinned base-change lemmas. It carries σ to the base change of TauCeti.DynkinType.typeAGraphAut (2n): both are based automorphisms reversing the simple roots, and an automorphism of a spanning system is determined by the simple roots. In that model the roots are e_a−e_b and the graph automorphism is the displayed σ. A root e_a−e_b with neither index central gives ±(f_i−f_j), ±(f_i+f_j) or the fixed root ±f_i. A pair of roots meeting the central index n+1 also sums to ±f_i. These cases exhaust all roots.

The f_i are orthogonal. Thus the listed set is closed under its reflections, has the B_n Cartan matrix, and the stated base has the required signed integral expansions. This verifies the finite reduced crystallographic root axioms directly.
For i<n the simple orbit is orthogonal. For the middle adjacent orbit, α_n+α_(n+1)=f_n has squared norm 2 rather than 4. Compute its coroot by the Euclidean pairing formula.
For an invariant weight with original simple-coroot values d_i=d_(2n+1−i), the folded simple-coroot values are d_i (i<n) and 2d_n.

nodes.title: Simple orbits of a based automorphism of an irreducible root system
nodes.statement: Let Φ be a nonempty irreducible finite reduced crystallographic real root system with base Δ, and τ a based automorphism, so that τ permutes Δ preserving every Cartan entry. (a) If Φ is not simply laced, τ fixes every simple root and is therefore the identity. (b) If Φ is simply laced, either every simple τ-orbit consists of pairwise orthogonal simple roots, or Φ has type A_(2n) for some n≥1 and τ acts on the Bourbaki-numbered simple roots as the reversal α_i ↦ α_(2n+1−i). In the second case {α_n,α_(n+1)} is the only simple orbit containing two nonorthogonal roots, and the other orbits {α_i,α_(2n+1−i)} are orthogonal.
hypotheses: Finite reduced crystallographic real root system Φ spanning E, irreducible and nonempty, with base Δ.
τ is a root-pairing automorphism whose index permutation maps the simple support onto itself.
proofSteps: On Δ, τ is an automorphism of the Dynkin diagram preserving all Cartan entries, hence root lengths; the diagram is a finite tree. Distinct nonadjacent simple roots have Cartan entry zero and are orthogonal.

Part (a): in types B_n, C_n, F4 and G2 the diagram is a path, whose only automorphisms are the identity and the reversal. The reversal either moves the unique multiple edge onto a simple edge or exchanges its two endpoints of different lengths, so it is not Cartan-preserving. Hence τ fixes Δ, which spans E, so τ is the identity.

Part (b): a tree automorphism preserves the center of the tree, a vertex or an edge. If τ fixes a vertex c, it preserves the distance to c; adjacent vertices of a tree lie at distances from c that differ by one, so no τ-orbit contains two adjacent simple roots, and every simple orbit is orthogonal.

Otherwise the center is an edge whose endpoints τ exchanges, and the diagram is two exchanged isomorphic halves joined by it. Every valid type other than A has exactly one branch node (D, E) or exactly one multiple edge (B, C, F4, G2), which such a symmetry would duplicate. So the type is A_m, the path has a central edge only for m=2n, and the only path automorphism exchanging it is the reversal.

The type is read off through existsUnique_dynkinType and its relabelling; under any relabelling, τ becomes a member of the numbered symmetry group, by the entrywise criterion. The reversal commutes with itself, so the conclusion does not depend on the relabelling chosen.

It is the orthogonal direct sum of the return-map folds transported by D on component cycles. Every positive folded root is the sum of a positive root orbit. nodes.title: Coroot step with central directions retained
nodes.statement: Let P be a finite reduced crystallographic real root pairing in finite-dimensional perfectly paired weight spaces V,V*, not necessarily spanned by the roots. Let σ be a P-automorphism preserving the base, and let λ,μ in a σ-stable subgroup L⊆V be fixed, dominant, integral on simple coroots, and distinct with μ−λ∈Q⁺. Assume Q⊆L. Then the conclusion of invariant-step holds in V. Apply P=the flipped real root pairing of a reductive root datum to obtain the integral positive-COROOT orbit step on its actual cocharacter lattice, preserving the common central component.
hypotheses: Finiteness, reducedness and crystallographicity concern the root set.
The ambient pairing is perfect; the induced finite root system on its real span has the canonical positive form. No finite-order assumption on σ on extra central directions is imposed.
proofSteps: Put E=span_R Φ and Z=the common kernel of all simple-coroot functionals. The symmetrized Cartan form is positive definite on E, hence the simple-coroot evaluation matrix on its simple basis is nonsingular. Solve this finite linear system to get V=E⊕Z and projection p preserving every simple-coroot evaluation. This uses only root-span positivity; it does not assert the canonical form is positive definite on V.
The decomposition is σ-stable: σ preserves roots and their coroot pairings. Thus pλ,pμ are fixed and retain the endpoint simple-coroot values. Since μ−λ∈E, pμ−pλ=μ−λ≠0.
Apply invariant-step on E with its full integral weight subgroup. The projected endpoints need not belong to the original L; their integral coroot values are all that is used.

The resulting increment β is in Q⊆L. Adding it to the ORIGINAL λ keeps the Z-component and lies below the ORIGINAL μ with the same integral difference budget. All simple-coroot values agree with those on E.

For a cocharacter lattice apply the entire construction to the dual pairing and the dual base. Work on the real span only inside this proof; the output is the sum of actual coroots in the original lattice.

For a σ-stable lattice with torsion, such as the inertia coinvariants X_*(T)_I that ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4 orders by its coweight dominance, apply the theorem to the image modulo torsion in X_*(T)_I⊗R. The coefficient budget of μ−λ lies in the free coroot lattice, which maps injectively to the real span, and the increment is a sum of actual coroots. So λ plus that increment lies in the original lattice, is σ-fixed and dominant, and satisfies both cone comparisons there.
